result.issue: What can Harbor customers do today with export scheduling, what are its current limits, and what improvements are planned?

questions.text: What can Harbor customers do today with export scheduling, what are its current limits, and what improvements are planned?

answers.text:
Harbor workspace administrators can schedule a recurring CSV export of completed orders from the reporting page. The scheduler is available to all paid workspaces as of the September release. Each schedule sends a download link to the administrator
A workspace may maintain up to five active export schedules. A schedule runs at most once per day, using the workspace time zone. The current CSV contains completed orders only; pending and cancelled orders are excluded.
The reporting group has approved work to add weekly and monthly cadence choices and to include cancelled orders as an optional export filter. Both items are planned for the next reporting cycle; neither has shipped.

source_excerpts.quote: Harbor workspace administrators can schedule a recurring CSV export of completed orders from the reporting page. The scheduler is available to all paid workspaces as of the September release. Each schedule sends a download link to the administrator who created it; the link expires after seven days. Scheduling does not grant access to other reports, and the recipient still needs an active workspace account to download the file.

The team considers a schedule active once its first delivery has been queued. Workspace owners can pause or delete a schedule from the same page. Pausing keeps the configuration, while deleting it removes the configuration and its delivery history from the page.

A workspace may maintain up to five active export schedules. A schedule runs at most once per day, using the workspace time zone. The current CSV contains completed orders only; pending and cancelled orders are excluded.

The delivery service retries a failed send twice over the following hour. A workspace administrator can check the most recent delivery result in the reporting page, but individual download events are not currently shown there.

The reporting group has approved work to add weekly and monthly cadence choices and to include cancelled orders as an optional export filter. Both items are planned for the next reporting cycle; neither has shipped. The group has also recorded a request for an API to create schedules, but no decision or target date exists for that request.

result.issue: How does Orchard handle a supplier invoice from receipt through approval and payment, and who owns each stage?

questions.text: How does Orchard handle a supplier invoice from receipt through approval and payment, and who owns each stage?

answers.text:
At Orchard, the accounts payable coordinator receives supplier invoices in the shared invoice mailbox. The coordinator checks that each invoice names a supplier and purchase order, then enters it in the ledger with status Received. Missing purchase
The budget owner compares the invoice amount with the purchase order and confirms that the goods or services were received. If both checks pass, the owner marks the invoice Approved in the ledger. A mismatch is sent back to accounts payable for
The treasury specialist includes approved invoices in the next Thursday payment run, provided the due date falls within the next fourteen days. Treasury sends the payment and records the payment reference in the ledger. An approved invoice outside
At Orchard, the accounts payable coordinator receives supplier invoices in the shared invoice mailbox. The coordinator checks that each invoice names a supplier and purchase order, then enters it in the ledger with status Received. Missing purchase

source_excerpts.quote: At Orchard, the accounts payable coordinator receives supplier invoices in the shared invoice mailbox. The coordinator checks that each invoice names a supplier and purchase order, then enters it in the ledger with status Received. Missing purchase order details are returned to the supplier for correction; the invoice does not enter the approval queue until corrected.
For invoices with complete intake details, the coordinator attaches the original invoice to the ledger record and routes the record to the budget owner named on the purchase order.

The budget owner compares the invoice amount with the purchase order and confirms that the goods or services were received. If both checks pass, the owner marks the invoice Approved in the ledger. A mismatch is sent back to accounts payable for investigation, rather than being approved automatically.

Approval is the budget owner's decision. Accounts payable maintains the record and communicates with the supplier during an investigation, but does not substitute its own approval for the owner's decision.

The treasury specialist includes approved invoices in the next Thursday payment run, provided the due date falls within the next fourteen days. Treasury sends the payment and records the payment reference in the ledger. An approved invoice outside that window stays approved until a later eligible run.
A weekly reconciliation checks payment references against the bank statement. The treasury specialist resolves discrepancies with accounts payable.

result.issue: What are the eligibility rules and process for Lumen’s customer credit, and how is the credit applied and tracked?

questions.text: What are the eligibility rules and process for Lumen’s customer credit, and how is the credit applied and tracked?

answers.text:
Lumen offers a service credit when a paid customer's production workspace is unavailable for more than four consecutive hours due to a Lumen service incident. The credit is ten percent of the workspace's monthly subscription charge. The rule is for
A customer submits a credit request through the support portal, including the affected workspace and incident date. Support verifies the incident window against the incident record and checks the request date. If eligible, support approves the
Billing applies an approved service credit to the affected workspace's next subscription invoice. The credit reduces that invoice's amount due and is not paid out as cash. Billing records the amount and support request identifier on the invoice
A customer submits a credit request through the support portal, including the affected workspace and incident date. Support verifies the incident window against the incident record and checks the request date. If eligible, support approves the

source_excerpts.quote: Lumen offers a service credit when a paid customer's production workspace is unavailable for more than four consecutive hours because of a Lumen service incident. Planned maintenance announced at least 48 hours ahead and outages caused solely by the customer's configuration are excluded. The credit equals ten percent of that workspace's monthly subscription charge.
The rule applies to the affected workspace, not every workspace owned by the customer. A customer must request a credit within thirty days of the incident ending.

A customer submits a credit request through the support portal, including the affected workspace and incident date. Support verifies the incident window against the incident record and checks the request date. If eligible, support approves the request and forwards it to billing; if ineligible, support explains the reason in the portal.
The portal records the outcome and a link to the incident record so the support team can follow the decision later.

Billing applies an approved service credit to the affected workspace's next subscription invoice. The credit reduces that invoice's amount due and is not paid out as cash. Billing records the amount and support request identifier on the invoice adjustment.
If the next invoice is smaller than the credit, the unused balance carries forward to the following subscription invoice for the same workspace.

questions.text: When will Cedar’s new customer portal launch, who owns the launch, and what is confirmed about its scope?

answers.text:
The operations update lists October 25 as the customer portal launch target, while the product update mentions October 18 as the target. However, neither document confirms the final launch date, as the updates do not record a final launch decision.
Mira Chen is named as the launch readiness coordinator in both the operations update and the product update, indicating she is responsible for the launch.
The Cedar customer portal is intended to let customers view their open support cases and update contact details. The product group has signed off those two capabilities for the first release.
The operations update mentions October 25 as the launch target, while the product update lists October 18 as the target. The product update also mentions an internal preview running with employees, which is not evidence of a customer launch.

The product update says the customer portal launch is targeted for October 18. It names Mira Chen, the product lead, as the person coordinating launch readiness. The date was a target in this update, and the update does not record a final launch decision.
